library(tidyverse)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(rstatix)
library(ggpubr)
library(patchwork)
# -----------------------------
# 1. Load data
# -----------------------------
data_raw <- read.csv("temp1_granular_module_metrics.csv")

# Ensure categorical variables are factors
data_raw$model <- factor(data_raw$model)
data_raw$style <- factor(data_raw$style)

# -----------------------------
# 2. Collapse 3 runs per module/config
#    into one robust value using median
# -----------------------------
data <- data_raw %>%
  group_by(module, model, style) %>%
  mutate(run_id = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

data_base <- data %>% 
  filter(style == "base")

data_combined <- data %>% 
  filter(style == "combined")

# -----------------------------
# 5. DAN box plot: DAN results by model
# -----------------------------
ggplot(data_base, aes(x = model, y = diff_dan, fill = model)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "DAN Comparison by Model & Base",
    x = "Model",
    y = "DAN"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
  
ggplot(data_combined, aes(x = model, y = diff_dan, fill = model)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "DAN Comparison by Model & Combined",
    x = "Model",
    y = "DAN"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
  
ggplot(data, aes(x = model, y = diff_dan, fill = model)) +

  theme_minimal() +

#####################
# PROMPT COMPARISON COMBINED BOX PLOT
#####################
data_clean <- data %>%
  mutate(diff_dan = as.numeric(diff_dan)) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(diff_dan, diff_coverage, diff_total_tests, diff_passing_tests, diff_failing_tests),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    style = str_to_title(style), 
    metric_label = case_when(
      metric == "diff_dan" ~ "DAN",
      metric == "diff_coverage" ~ "Coverage",
      metric == "diff_total_tests" ~ "Total Tests",
      metric == "diff_passing_tests" ~ "Passing Tests",
      metric == "diff_failing_tests" ~ "Failing Tests"
    )
  )

shared_theme <- theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#e0e0e0", color = "black"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

p1 <- data_clean %>%
  filter(metric_label %in% c("DAN", "Coverage", "Total Tests")) %>%
  mutate(metric_label = factor(metric_label, levels = c("DAN", "Coverage", "Total Tests"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = style, y = value, fill = style)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.85, width = 0.6, color = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_grid(metric_label ~ ., scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Base" = "#7cc9eb", "Combined" = "#fdbf33")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Metric Score") +
  shared_theme

p2 <- data_clean %>%
  filter(metric_label %in% c("Passing Tests", "Failing Tests")) %>%
  mutate(metric_label = factor(metric_label, levels = c("Passing Tests", "Failing Tests"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = style, y = value, fill = style)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.85, width = 0.6, color = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_grid(metric_label ~ ., scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Base" = "#7cc9eb", "Combined" = "#fdbf33")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  shared_theme

final_plot <- (p1 | (plot_spacer() / p2 / plot_spacer() + plot_layout(heights = c(0.3, 2.4, 0.3)))) + 
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Comparison of Metrics by Prompt",
    caption = "Prompt Style",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(t = 20))
    )
  )

print(final_plot)

ggsave("prompt_comparison_final.pdf", plot = final_plot, width = 10, height = 12, dpi = 300)

data_long_comb <- data %>%
  mutate(diff_dan = as.numeric(diff_dan)) %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(diff_dan, diff_coverage, diff_total_tests, diff_passing_tests, diff_failing_tests),

  ) %>%
  mutate(
    style = toupper(style),
    metric_label = case_when(
      metric == "diff_dan" ~ "DAN",

final_comb_plot <- ggplot(data_long_comb, aes(x = model, y = value, fill = style)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.85, width = 0.7, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8, 
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) + 
  facet_grid(metric_label ~ ., scales = "free_y") + 
  theme_bw(base_size = 15) +

    y = "Metric Score",

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

  )

ggsave("model_prompt_comparison.pdf", plot = final_comb_plot, width = 15, height = 20, dpi = 300)



#################################################################
################# DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS ########################
#################################################################

# Define the metrics we want to analyze
metrics_to_stats <- c("diff_dan", "diff_coverage", "diff_total_tests", 
                      "diff_passing_tests", "diff_failing_tests")

# Define the columns we want in our final tables
desired_columns <- c("variable", "n", "mean", "sd", "median", "q1", "q3")

# 1. Summary stats by Model
stats_by_model <- data %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  get_summary_stats(all_of(metrics_to_stats), type = "full") %>%
  select(model, all_of(desired_columns))

# 2. Summary stats by Prompt Style
stats_by_style <- data %>%
  group_by(style) %>%
  get_summary_stats(all_of(metrics_to_stats), type = "full") %>%
  select(style, all_of(desired_columns))

# 3. Combined: Summary stats by Model AND Prompt Style
stats_combined <- data %>%
  group_by(model, style) %>%
  get_summary_stats(all_of(metrics_to_stats), type = "full") %>%
  select(model, style, all_of(desired_columns))

# --- Printing Results ---
cat("\n--- STATS BY MODEL ---\n")
print(stats_by_model, n = Inf) # n = Inf ensures all metrics are shown

cat("\n--- STATS BY PROMPT STYLE ---\n")
print(stats_by_style, n = Inf)

cat("\n--- COMBINED STATS (MODEL x STYLE) ---\n")
print(stats_combined, n = Inf)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define the specific target modules
# ---------------------------------------------------------
target_modules <- c(
  "decorators.py", "packages.py", "cmd.py", "headers.py", 
  "httpie.base.py", "py_backwards.base.py", "dict_unpacking.py", 
  "return_from_generator.py", "yield_from.py", "journaling.py", "python.py"
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Filter and calculate mean for these modules per model
# ---------------------------------------------------------
stats_specific_modules <- data %>%
  # Filter the dataset for only the modules in our target list
  filter(module %in% target_modules) %>%
  # Group by model to see how each performed on these specific files
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_coverage_diff = mean(diff_coverage, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Including n helps verify how many data points (runs) were included
    n_observations = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# --- Print the results ---
cat("\n--- MEAN COVERAGE DIFF (Target Modules Only) ---\n")
print(stats_specific_modules)

# Pivot data to long format for easy faceting
data_long <- data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("diff_"), 
    names_to = "metric",

# Create one comprehensive plot
ggplot(data_long, aes(x = model, y = value, fill = style)) +

# Summary stats for the Composite Score by Model
stats_by_model <- data %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  get_summary_stats(composite_score, type = "median_iqr")

# Summary stats for the Composite Score by Prompt Style
stats_by_style <- data_module %>%
  group_by(style) %>%
  get_summary_stats(composite_score, type = "median_iqr")

print(stats_by_model)
print(stats_by_style)

# -----------------------------
# 11. Mann-Whitney U with Explicit Holm Adjustment
# -----------------------------

# Comparison across Models using Holm-Bonferroni
stat_test_model <- data_module %>%
  wilcox_test(composite_score ~ model) %>%
  # Explicitly setting the adjustment method to "holm"
  adjust_pvalue(method = "holm") %>% 
  add_significance() %>%
  add_xy_position(x = "model")

# Comparison across Prompt Styles
# (Since there are only 2 groups here, Holm adjustment has no effect)
stat_test_style <- data_module %>%
  wilcox_test(composite_score ~ style) %>%
  adjust_pvalue(method = "holm") %>%
  add_significance() %>%
  add_xy_position(x = "style")

print(stat_test_model)
print(stat_test_style)
  
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Friedman Test: Models (Base Prompt Style Only)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Filtering only for the 'base' style to find the strongest baseline model
data_base <- data_module %>% 
  filter(style == "base")

print(data_base)

res.fried_base <- data_base %>% 
  friedman_test(composite_score ~ model | module)

res.fried_base_b <- friedman.test(composite_score ~ model, data = data_base %>% select(model, composite_score))

ggplot(data_base, aes(y = composite_score, x = model, fill = model)) +
 geom_boxplot(width = 0.5) +
 theme_bw()

print("--- Friedman Test (Base Prompt Only) ---")
print(res.fried_base)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Pairwise Comparisons (Post-hoc for Models)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Performing Wilcoxon (Mann-Whitney equivalent for paired data)
pwc_base <- data_base %>%
  wilcox_test(composite_score ~ model, paired = TRUE, p.adjust.method = "holm") %>%
  add_significance()

print("--- Pairwise Comparisons (Base Prompt) ---")
print(pwc_base)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Acknowledge the "Best" Model
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Identifying the model with the lowest median penalty score
best_model_name <- data_base %>% 
  group_by(model) %>% 
  summarise(median_penalty = median(composite_score)) %>% 
  arrange(median_penalty) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  pull(model)

cat("The statistically identified best model is:", as.character(best_model_name), "\n")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Vargha-Delaney A12 for Significant Pairs
# ---------------------------------------------------------
if (!require("effsize")) install.packages("effsize")
library(effsize)

# Filter the pairs that were statistically significant (p.adj < 0.05)
significant_pairs <- pwc_base %>% filter(p.adj < 0.05)

if(nrow(significant_pairs) > 0) {
  for(i in 1:nrow(significant_pairs)) {
    m1 <- significant_pairs$group1[i]
    m2 <- significant_pairs$group2[i]
    
    pair_data <- data_base %>% filter(model %in% c(m1, m2)) %>% mutate(model = factor(model))
    res_vda <- VD.A(composite_score ~ model, data = pair_data)
    
    cat("\nEffect Size for", m1, "vs", m2, ":\n")
    print(res_vda)
  }
} else {
  cat("\nNo pairs were statistically significant after Holm adjustment in the Base-only subset.\n")
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Prompt Analysis for the Best Model
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Comparing Base vs Combined specifically for the best model (Mini)
data_best_model <- data_module %>% 
  filter(model == best_model_name)

res.prompt_comparison <- data_best_model %>% 
  wilcox_test(composite_score ~ style, paired = TRUE) %>%
  add_significance()

print(paste("--- Prompt Style Comparison for", best_model_name, "---"))
print(res.prompt_comparison)

# -----------------------------
# 19. DAN Metric: Friedman Test (Step 1)
# -----------------------------

# We use the same block_id (module + style) to account for module difficulty
res.fried_dan <- data_module %>% 
  friedman_test(diff_dan ~ model | block_id)

print("--- Friedman Test: DAN Metric ---")
print(res.fried_dan)

# -----------------------------
# 20. DAN Metric: Pairwise Wilcoxon (Step 2)
# -----------------------------

# We check pairs to see if any specific model is better at DAN
pwc_dan <- data_module %>%
  wilcox_test(diff_dan ~ model, paired = TRUE, p.adjust.method = "holm") %>%
  add_significance()

print("--- Pairwise Paired Wilcoxon: DAN Metric ---")
print(pwc_dan)

# -----------------------------
# 21. DAN Metric: Effect Size (Step 3)
# -----------------------------

# Checking the probability of one model beating another in DAN
# Example: Claude vs. Mini
ds_dan_vda <- data_module %>% 
  filter(model %in% c("claude", "mini")) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model))

res.vda_dan <- VD.A(diff_dan ~ model, data = ds_dan_vda)
print(res.vda_dan)

# Total test count penalty
ggplot(data_module, aes(x = model, y = n_test_change, fill = style)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1") +
  labs(
    title = "Normalized Total Test Count Penalty by Model and Prompt Style",
    subtitle = "Lower is better (closer to 0 original test-count difference)",
    x = "Model",
    y = "Normalized Total Test Count Penalty",
    fill = "Prompt Style"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Passing tests penalty
ggplot(data_module, aes(x = model, y = n_pass_change, fill = style)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1") +
  labs(
    title = "Normalized Passing Test Penalty by Model and Prompt Style",
    subtitle = "Lower is better (closer to 0 original passing-test difference)",
    x = "Model",
    y = "Normalized Passing Test Penalty",
    fill = "Prompt Style"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Failing tests penalty

ggplot(data_module, aes(x = model, y = n_fail_change, fill = style)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1") +
  labs(
    title = "Failing Test Comparison by Model and Prompt Style",
    subtitle = "Lower is better (closer to 0 original failing-test difference)",
    x = "Model",
    y = "Failing Test",
    fill = "Prompt Style"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
# -----------------------------
# 3. Normalization function
#    Min-max scaling to [0, 1]
# -----------------------------
normalize <- function(x) {
  if (max(x, na.rm = TRUE) == min(x, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    return(rep(0, length(x)))
  }
  (x - min(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / (max(x, na.rm = TRUE) - min(x, na.rm = TRUE))
}
  # -----------------------------
# 4. Create normalized metric penalties
#    Lower = better for every metric
# -----------------------------
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    # Closer to 0 is better -> use absolute deviation from 0
    n_cov_change   = normalize(abs(diff_coverage)),
    n_test_change  = normalize(abs(diff_total_tests)),
    n_pass_change  = normalize(abs(diff_passing_tests)),
    n_fail_change  = normalize(abs(diff_failing_tests)),
    n_dan_penalty  = normalize(-diff_dan),
    composite_score = n_cov_change +
                      n_test_change +
                      n_pass_change +
                      n_fail_change
                      )

# Optional: inspect summary
summary(data_module$composite_score)

# -----------------------------
# 8. Normalized drill-down plots for each metric
#    Every plot is now lower-is-better
# -----------------------------

# Coverage penalty
ggplot(data_module, aes(x = model, y = n_cov_change, fill = style)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1") +
  labs(
    title = "Difference in Coverage Comparison by Model and Prompt Style",
    x = "Model",
    y = "Coverage",
    fill = "Prompt Style"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# DAN penalty
ggplot(data_module, aes(x = model, y = n_dan_penalty, fill = style)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1") +
  labs(
    title = "Difference in DAN Comparison by Model and Prompt Style",
    x = "Model",
    y = "DAN",
    fill = "Prompt Style"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
